source_text: Nam hoc quod ait, abstinere a cibis docendum fore, non utique apud prudentem arguit Christianorum parcitatem, aut denuntiat posse existere homines qui inediae discrimen indicant; sed ostendit, quoniam cum exorirentur, qui dicerent animalia omnia victibus a Deo creata mortalium, quia de concupiscentia et commixtione sexus nascerentur, diabolico malo esse polluta, quid consequeretur expressit, videlicet renuntiandum esse alimentis, si eorum propagatio diabolica crederetur. Unde et tu hanc infamationem commixtionis corporum ab animalibus removes, ut subsistat ratio simulandi. Homines tamen qui ad imaginem Dei facti sunt, propter hanc ipsam concupiscentiam generantium, dicis ad ius daemonis pertinere. Ambo igitur, tu et Manichaeus unam habetis causam substantiarum vituperandarum et transcribendarum diabolo; sed ille propter hanc affectionem quae sentitur in naturali opere, universas damnat animantes; tu autem non omnes, sed quod est foedius, meliores. Absolvis enim sues, canes, et asinos, ut Manichaeos vitare videaris; sed damnas, propter hoc idem quod Manichaeus, omnes homines qui ad imaginem Dei facti sunt; ac nusquam malum naturale constituens nisi in imagine Dei, concionaris contra nos, accusator sanctorum et patronus asinorum.
pass_a_gloss: For this which he says, that it would be taught to abstain from foods, does not indeed with a prudent person accuse the sparingness of Christians, or denounce that humans can exist who declare the crisis of starvation; but he showed, because when there would arise those who would say that all animals created by God for the foods of mortals, because they would be born from desire and mingling of sex, were polluted by diabolical evil, he expressed what would follow, namely that foods must be renounced if their propagation were believed diabolical. Whence you also remove this infamation of the mingling of bodies from animals, so that the reason of pretending may stand. Humans nevertheless who were made to the image of God, on account of this very desire of those generating, you say belong to the demon's right. Both therefore, you and Manichaeus, have one cause of blaming substances and transferring them to the devil; but he, on account of this affection which is felt in the natural work, condemns all living beings; you however not all, but what is fouler, the better ones. For you acquit swine, dogs, and asses, so that you may seem to avoid the Manichaeans; but you condemn, on account of this same thing as Manichaeus, all humans who were made to the image of God; and nowhere establishing natural evil except in the image of God, you harangue against us, accuser of the holy and patron of asses.

Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: When he says that abstinence from foods will be taught, an intelligent reader understands that he is not accusing Christian restraint or announcing the possible appearance of people who prescribe the ordeal of fasting (compare 1 Timothy 4:1–4). Rather, he shows that people would arise who said that all the animals God created for mortals’ food were polluted by the devil’s evil because they were born through desire and sexual union. He then expressed the consequence: foods must be renounced if their reproduction is believed devilish. That is why you remove this slander against bodily union from animals, so that your pretense can survive. Yet you say that human beings, made in God’s image, belong to the demon’s jurisdiction because of this very desire in those who beget them (compare Genesis 1:26–27). Both you and Manichaeus therefore have one reason for disparaging substances and transferring them to the devil. But he condemns every animal because of this feeling experienced in a natural act; you condemn not all, but—what is uglier—the better ones. You acquit pigs, dogs, and donkeys to appear to avoid the Manichaeans. But for the very same reason as Manichaeus you condemn all human beings, who were made in God’s image. Placing natural evil nowhere except in God’s image, you declaim against us as accuser of the saints and defender of donkeys (1 Timothy 4:1–4) (Genesis 1:26–27).

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian defends marital union (commixtio) as God's work, not the devil's property.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
